tus.notes: GFZE01 .sdata 0x801A6400 gives the mmu.c filename. The page-table setup and update paths call the lookup at 0x800077E0, slot allocation at 0x80007730, segment-register read at 0x80007654 and PTE/TLB helpers at 0x80007664 and 0x80007700. Both lookup and allocation use the SDR1 helper at 0x800079A0 and the primary/secondary hash helpers at 0x800079C4 and 0x80007A00. The next routine, 0x80007A44, instead initializes a color value at 0x801A6408 and calls rendering routines 0x800744F8 and 0x80008204. The end of mmu.c is inferred from this subsystem break; the next TU is not named here.

0x80007A44..0x80007CDC: no donor: these five functions share the clear color at .sdata 0x801A6408 and the flag at .sbss 0x801A6728. Their three .sdata2 color initializers end at 0x801A6F0C and the next TU starts on the 8-byte boundary 0x801A6F10; one compile packs the next literal at 0x801A6F0C. The file name is a placeholder.

0x80007CDC..0x80008E34: no donor: unnamed .sdata2 literals are per TU, and 0x801A6F14 is shared by 0x80007F70, 0x80008204 and 0x800084E8, 0x801A6F38 by 0x80008204 and 0x800084E8, 0x801A6F30 by 0x800084E8 and 0x80008C20. Only 0x800081C8 calls 0x80007F70 and only 0x800084E8 calls 0x800087F4 and 0x80008A4C. 0x80008E30 is empty in USA, absent in Japan and a real function in PAL that reads this TU's literal 0x801A6F20. 0x80007CDC, 0x80007D58, 0x80008BA8, 0x80008BEC and 0x80008DB4 have no data evidence and are placed by position. The file name is a placeholder.

0x80008E34..0x80009FBC: no donor: a modified SDK OSAlloc with its OSCheckHeap failure strings, sharing the heap state at .sbss 0x801A6730..0x801A6748 and .sdata 0x801A6410/0x801A6414. It ends at PPCArch.c. The sizes are this build's.

0x8003E9EC reads .sdata2 0x801A71C8..0x801A71D8, which repeats the 2^52 conversion constant of perf.c at 0x801A71C0, so it is the first function of this TU.

GFZE01 fn_8004F7F8 is a 0x20-byte DCInvalidateRange wrapper. GQNE5D libadxgca.a adx_fcch.o (mk-deception map 33b1e00) has the same-sized ADXF_Ocbi at 0x802D0D64 as its only function, immediately before adx_fs.o. This is comparative ownership evidence, not a GX linker map.

GX starts this range with partition/file-ID validation: fn_8004F818 references .rodata 0x80091258 and 0x8009127C. GFZE01 ADXF_ExecServer and the current symbol ADXT_DestroyAll both iterate the file table at .bss 0x80186B68 with stride 0x44; the latter calls fn_8004FC94, which references the ADXF_Stop diagnostic at .rodata 0x800912A0. GQNE5D libadxgca.a adx_fs.o (mk-deception map 33b1e00) holds ADXF_ExecServer (0x190), ADXF_CloseAll (0x5C), and ADXF_Close (0x2DC vs GX 0x2D4) in that order. The next GX function, fn_8004FF68, scans compressed-stream sync words via a bit reader and its own mask table. Text ownership is inferred; the shared table and literals are evidence, not section ownership transfers.

The SJ bit reader. Its .bss 0x80186FA8..0x8018710C ends four bytes before the next TU on the 8-byte boundary 0x80187110; one compile would place the next object at 0x8018710C. 0x80050670 reads the table just before this TU's mask table in .data.
Subband decoding. Uses .bss 0x80187110..0x80187370 and .rodata 0x800912F0..0x80091300. Its end is inferred from the change to the ADXT attach wrappers at 0x80051CC0.
ADXT attach and detach wrappers; 0x80051E64 owns the "E1052501 ADXT_AttachAHX" strings at .rodata 0x80091300.
The 32-point transform. It reads its own 0.0f at .rodata 0x80091330; the next TU repeats that value at 0x80091338, so the two cannot be one compile.
16 generated synthesis routines over .rodata 0x80091338..0x80091350, which repeats the 2^52 conversion constant of ahx_decode.c. The 8-byte 0x80053A30 has no data and stays with this run.
Creates and frees the synthesis objects. Uses .bss 0x80187370..0x801873D8 and the 2^31 literal at .rodata 0x80091350, which repeats a value of ahx_synth.c. Its .rodata ends at 0x80091354.

The AHX player. Its "AHX/GC Ver.1.24" string starts on the 8-byte TU boundary 0x80091358, and one compile with the literal above packs it at 0x80091354. Uses .bss 0x801873D8..0x80187430. The two getters at 0x80053EA0 and 0x80053EA8 read player fields.
GX sizes from 0x8005466C equal GQNE5D cri_cvfs.o in order, without cvFsGetFileSize (0x4A4), which GX does not link. .bss 0x80187430 is first used at 0x8005466C.

All six GX functions have the same ordered sizes as GQNE5D libadxgca.a rna_res.o (0x802D9110..0x802D9540; mk-deception map 33b1e0082c7630ee4f20b828559966872ae670e1). The last two are the paired ARAM resource teardown/setup: both use the state at 0x80192BD0 and the adjacent 32-entry table at 0x80192BE4. The preceding wrapper 0x8005BE48 calls fn_8005A614 and belongs to ax_rna.c. This evidence bounds .text; data splits remain separate.

.sdata2 0x801A7218..0x801A7280 and .rodata 0x800929D8..0x80092B38. The pitch table at 0x800929D8 is repeated at 0x80092B38 by the next TU. 0x8005FBDC..0x8006060C hold no literals: they are placed here because the next TU's track array is first used at 0x8006060C.
Every user of the 0x540-byte track array 0x80192D68 lies in this range. .sdata2 0x801A7280..0x801A7318 repeats the previous TU's literals.

.sdata2 0x801A7318..0x801A7328 repeats the 2^52 conversion constant. It addresses the effect work areas at .bss 0x801932A8..0x80193B08 one symbol at a time, as externs of sasnd_core.c. The end of the TU is not bounded by data.

MIDI-style control dispatch, voice lookup and the program-change loaders over the state at 0x801A6C80. The band has no literals or private data, so neither end is bounded by data: it follows the effect routine and stops at the loader of sasnd_core.c. All 19 functions build as one compile under one set of flags.

Owns .bss 0x801932A8..0x80199670 and .sbss 0x801A6C78..0x801A6C88: 0x80067DE4 addresses the effect work areas off one section base, and 0x80068BFC initializes the state at 0x801A6C80 from .bss 0x80193B48. .rodata runs version string, loader strings, 0x80092C38 table (0x8006953C), wave table, so 0x80065F34..0x80069AE0 is one contribution. .sdata2 0x801A7328..0x801A7350.
.sdata2 0x801A7350..0x801A7370 repeats 20.0, 255.0, -960.0, 127.0, 10.0 and 2^52 from the earlier TUs. 0x80069B10 and 0x80069FCC are called only by 0x80069CE4. Ends at arc.c.
